public_rationale: The ordinary current-technology reading is supported. Developers report useful coding applications, while a broad evaluation finds recurrent serious errors in ordinary information tasks. Coding benefits vary, and perceived gains can be misleading. This does not establish an immutable inability to become reliable; the result depends on reading “inherently” as a characteristic weakness of available systems.
limitations: Reliability varies by task, model, safeguards, and verification.
The selected reporting period is 2025, not a comprehensive test of every system available on the post date.
A stronger claim about unavoidable unreliability remains unproved.

I use 2025, the latest complete calendar year before the post, as the reporting period for this ongoing state.
I assess systems then available. A claim that no future generative system could become reliable would require different evidence.

evidence.locator: AI → AI Agents, Impacts of AI agents
evidence.explanation: Developer respondents report useful applications in their work, supporting the modest assertion that practical coding uses exist. Self-selection and subjective productivity estimates limit the strength of this evidence.

Responses generated in late May and early June across four assistants and multiple languages contained significant problems in 45% of cases. The report also records improvement in the comparable BBC subset, so persistent problems do not imply no progress.

In this experiment, experienced developers working on familiar repositories became slower despite believing AI helped. This limits reliance on perceived productivity and broad claims of coding gains, but does not negate the existence of some useful applications.
